/-!
# Erdős Problem 505

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/505](https://www.erdosproblems.com/505)

**Borsuk's conjecture** (1933): Is every bounded set of diameter 1 in $\mathbb{R}^n$
the union of at most $n + 1$ sets of diameter strictly less than 1?

Erdős [Er44] suspected this is false for sufficiently large $n$. Confirmed
by Kahn–Kalai [KK93], who disproved the conjecture for $n \geq 2015$.
The current best is $n \geq 64$ (Jenrich–Brouwer, 2014).

The conjecture is true for $n \leq 3$ (Eggleston [Eg55] for $n = 3$).

### References

- [Bo33] Borsuk, K. (1933). *Drei Sätze über die n-dimensionale euklidische Sphäre*.
  Fund. Math. 20, 177–190.
- [Er44] Erdős, P. (1944). Remarks on a conjecture of Borsuk.
- [Eg55] Eggleston, H. G. (1955). *Covering a three-dimensional set with sets of
  smaller diameter*. J. London Math. Soc. 30, 11–24.
- [KK93] Kahn, J., Kalai, G. (1993). *A counterexample to Borsuk's conjecture*.
  Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 29, 60–62.

### AI disclosure

Lean 4 code in this file was drafted with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).
The mathematical content and references are the author's own work.
-/

namespace Erdos505

@[category test, AMS 52]

    (S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)))
    (hS : Bornology.IsBounded S) (hd : 0 < diam S) :
    ∃ (F : Fin 2 → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))),
      S ⊆ ⋃ i, F i ∧ ∀ i, diam (F i) < diam S := by
  sorry

/-- **Erdős Problem 505** (disproved). Borsuk's conjecture is false for
sufficiently large $n$: there exists a dimension $n$ and a bounded set
$S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ with positive diameter such that $S$ cannot be
covered by $n + 1$ subsets each of diameter strictly less than $\operatorname{diam}(S)$.

Erdős [Er44] suspected this. Disproved by Kahn–Kalai [KK93] for
$n \geq 2015$. Currently known to be false for $n \geq 64$.
A formal proof was formalised by Boris Alexeev using Aristotle. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 52,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/96cd54930d844e3655e6bb89b96b65516397dae9/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos505.lean#L1153"]
theorem erdos_505 : ∃ (n : ℕ),
    ∃ (S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))),
      Bornology.IsBounded S ∧ 0 < diam S ∧
        ∀ (F : Fin (n + 1) → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))),
          S ⊆ ⋃ i, F i →
          ∃ i, diam S ≤ diam (F i) := by
  sorry

/-- **Borsuk's conjecture, small dimensions** (open / true for $n \leq 3$).
Every bounded set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ with $n \leq 3$ can be
covered by $n + 1$ subsets each of strictly smaller diameter.

Trivial for $n \leq 2$; proved for $n = 3$ by Eggleston [Eg55]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_505.small_dim (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 3)
    (S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))
    (hS : Bornology.IsBounded S) (hd : 0 < diam S) :
    ∃ (F : Fin (n + 1) → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))),
      S ⊆ ⋃ i, F i ∧ ∀ i, diam (F i) < diam S := by
  sorry

end Erdos505

findings.description: The covering family at lines 75–77 is unrestricted: `S ⊆ ⋃ i, F i` does not make the individual `F i` subsets of S or bounded. Mathlib's real-valued `Metric.diam` is zero on unbounded sets. Taking every `F i = Set.univ` therefore covers S but gives `diam (F i) = 0`, contradicting the required conclusion and `0 < diam S`. The same universe diameter is zero in dimension 0 because that space is a singleton. Consequently the entire existential statement is false, not a statement of the genuine counterexample to Borsuk's conjecture. `Review505.negation_of_main` in the scratch file proves its exact negation without using any sorry-backed theorem.
findings.source_evidence: Borsuk (1933), p. 190, asks whether a bounded subset E of R^n can be decomposed into n+1 sets each of smaller diameter (https://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/fm/fm20/fm20117.pdf). Kahn–Kalai's abstract and Introduction formulate the diameter-one partition problem and prove counterexamples (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/9307229). These are genuine smaller-diameter pieces, not unbounded supersets assigned a default real diameter of zero.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the covering premise `S ⊆ ⋃ i, F i` with `S = ⋃ i, F i`. Then each F i is a subset of bounded S, so `Metric.diam` has its intended meaning. Alternatively, explicitly restrict the quantified family by `∀ i, Bornology.IsBounded (F i)`, or use `Metric.ediam` for the diameter comparisons.

findings.description: The existential conclusion admits `F i = Set.univ`: the family covers S and every member has `Metric.diam = 0 < diam S`. It thus expresses a trivial covering property that holds in every dimension, without using `hn : n ≤ 3` or boundedness of S, rather than the geometric small-dimension theorem. Intersecting these witnesses with S does not repair their claimed diameter bound: the intersections are S itself. A sorry-free proof of the conclusion for arbitrary n is `Review505.trivial_cover`; the exact subsidiary statement is proved by `Review505.small_dim_trivially`.
findings.source_evidence: Kahn–Kalai, Introduction, explicitly records that Borsuk's partition assertion is proved in dimensions 2 and 3 (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/9307229); https://www.erdosproblems.com/505 credits Eggleston [Eg55] for the three-dimensional case. The assertion concerns genuinely smaller-diameter pieces of a bounded set.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `S ⊆ ⋃ i, F i` with `S = ⋃ i, F i` in the existential conclusion. Equivalently, retain the covering inclusion and require `∀ i, Bornology.IsBounded (F i) ∧ diam (F i) < diam S`, or use extended diameters.

findings.description: This test has the same invalid witnesses: both covering sets may be the whole Euclidean line, whose `Metric.diam` is zero. Thus the statement does not require a genuine split into two smaller-diameter pieces. Already for the bounded unit-diameter set `{0, EuclideanSpace.single 0 1}`, the whole line satisfies the Lean smaller-diameter inequality although its extended diameter is infinite. The exact test statement and this concrete disagreement are proved without sorry by `Review505.test_one_trivially` and `Review505.bogus_small_piece`.
findings.source_evidence: This declaration is the n=1 specialization of the bounded-set decomposition question in Borsuk (1933), p. 190 (https://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/fm/fm20/fm20117.pdf), equivalently the diameter-one partition question in Kahn–Kalai's Introduction (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/9307229). Its pieces must have actual diameter strictly less than that of S.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `S = ⋃ i, F i`, or explicitly require the two covering sets to be bounded, or replace the diameter comparisons with `Metric.ediam` comparisons.

findings.description: The module bibliography gives `[Er44] Erdős, P. (1944). Remarks on a conjecture of Borsuk`, and both the module and main theorem docstrings cite it for Erdős's suspicion. This is not the reference identified by the source. The source attributes the quotation to [Er81b], and Kahn–Kalai identifies the corresponding contribution as Erdős's 1981 `My Scottish book "problems"`. The Rényi bibliography's 1944 entries contain no paper with the title supplied here.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/505 says: `In [Er81b] Erdős wrote 'I suspect that it is false for sufficiently high dimensions'.` Kahn–Kalai, bibliography item A, cites P. Erdős, `My Scottish book "problems"`, The Scottish Book, Birkhäuser, 1981 (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/9307229). The 1944 publication list is at https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the unsupported [Er44] bibliography entry and its two uses with [Er81b], Erdős, `My Scottish Book 'Problems'`, The Scottish Book (1981).

demonstrated.claim: The exact statement is false because the constant universal-set cover forces diam S ≤ 0, contradicting positive diameter.
The exact statement is proved by taking every covering set to be Set.univ, without using the dimension bound or boundedness hypothesis.
The exact dimension-one test is proved by the same family consisting of two copies of Set.univ.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«505»

/-! The covering sets in Erdős 505 need not be bounded or contained in S.
Taking every covering set to be the whole space breaks all three statements' intent. -/

namespace Erdos505TrivialProof

-- Metric.diam sends infinite diameter to 0; dimension 0 is a singleton instead.
private theorem universe_diam (n : ℕ) :
    Metric.diam (Set.univ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) = 0 := by
  cases n with
  | zero => exact Metric.diam_subsingleton (fun x _ y _ => Subsingleton.elim x y)
  | succ n => exact Metric.diam_univ_of_noncompact

-- Erdos505.erdos_505: false, since F i = univ covers S but forces diam S ≤ 0.
theorem main_is_false : ¬ (type_of% @Erdos505.erdos_505) := by
  rintro ⟨n, S, _, hd, h⟩
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := h (fun _ => Set.univ) (by
    intro x _
    exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨(0 : Fin (n + 1)), Set.mem_univ x⟩)
  exact (not_le_of_gt hd) (by simpa only [universe_diam] using hi)

-- Erdos505.erdos_505.small_dim: F i = univ proves it without the dimension bound or hS.
theorem small_dim_is_trivial : type_of% @Erdos505.erdos_505.small_dim := by
  intro n _ S _ hd
  refine ⟨fun _ => Set.univ, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x _
    exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨(0 : Fin (n + 1)), Set.mem_univ x⟩
  · intro i
    simpa only [universe_diam] using hd

-- Erdos505.erdos_505.test_dim_one: the same two copies of univ pass this test.
theorem test_dim_one_is_trivial : type_of% @Erdos505.erdos_505.test_dim_one := by
  intro S hS hd
  exact small_dim_is_trivial 1 (by decide) S hS hd

#print axioms main_is_false
#print axioms small_dim_is_trivial
#print axioms test_dim_one_is_trivial

end Erdos505TrivialProof

submission.summary: Replaced the covering inclusion with `S = ⋃ i, F i` in all three declarations. Each piece is now a subset of bounded S, excluding the unbounded-set diameter loophole. Only the three statement lines were changed; compilation succeeds with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
